title: Occupancy Aggregation of Country Home Loans (Rural Home Loans)
content:
Home loans of the Rural Home Loans program are aggregated by occupancy.

## Rule

1. A member may hold no more Country Home loans of one occupancy than the product's loans-by-occupancy figure allows, counting loans in applied, active, forbearance or nonaccrual status (the count of the member's Country Home loans in those statuses, by occupancy).
2. A second Country Home loan of the same occupancy is not registered.
3. A member moving to a new primary residence applies for the new loan as a primary residence only once the old one is paid off or is re-certified as a second home by the credit officer.
4. A product limited to primary residences may not finance a second home.

## Basis of the check on a new application

- **Record relied on:** the loan records of the association, not the member's account of them, read before the application is registered.
- **Object compared:** the same member and the same occupancy as the application. A loan of that member and that occupancy in applied, active, forbearance or nonaccrual status makes the application a second loan of the same occupancy, whichever homesite parcel the new application names.
- **Statuses that count:** applied, active, forbearance, nonaccrual. A loan that is paid off or declined is not in a counted status.

## Points of judgement

- *Hypothetical case:* a member with an active primary-residence loan applies for a new primary-residence loan on another parcel. The record shows a counted loan of the same occupancy, so the second loan of that occupancy is not registered; the new primary-residence application may be made once the old loan is paid off or the credit officer has re-certified it as a second home.
- *Hypothetical case:* the same member applies instead for a second-home loan and holds no other second-home loan in a counted status. The occupancy of the application differs from the existing loan's, so the existing loan is no obstacle under this rule.
- The Country Home Jumbo 30-Year Fixed accepts primary residences only; as a product limited to primary residences it may not finance a second home.
